questions.question:
Convert the interrogative sentence into Indirect Speech:
The clerk said to the lawyer, "Is the registrar present in his chamber?"

options.text: The clerk asked the lawyer that if the registrar was present in his chamber.
The clerk asked the lawyer if the registrar was present in his chamber.
The clerk asked the lawyer if was the registrar present in his chamber.
The clerk enquired the lawyer whether the registrar is present in his chamber.

questions.explanation: Direct speech ka question auxiliary 'Is' se shuru ho raha hai (Yes/No question). Reporting verb 'said to' ko 'asked' mein badla aur connective 'if' lagaya. Indirect question statement order follow karta hai, isliye subject 'the registrar' pehle aayega aur past auxiliary 'was' baad mein aayegi. Option (B) bilkul correct hai. Option (A) mein fatal 'that if' double conjunction blunder hai. Option (C) mein auxiliary inversion 'was the registrar' retain kar liya gaya jo galat hai. Option (D) mein 'enquired' ke baad preposition 'of' missing hai aur tense backshift nahi kiya gaya.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Yes/No Question Transformation (If/Whether) & Inversion Removal.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.question:
Choose the correct Indirect form of the sentence:
The magistrate said to the witness, "Do you recognize the accused?"

options.text: The magistrate asked the witness if he recognized the accused.
The magistrate asked the witness if did he recognize the accused.
The magistrate asked that if he recognized the accused.
The magistrate told the witness whether he recognized the accused.

questions.explanation: Auxiliary 'Do' se start hone wale affirmative question ko Indirect Speech mein convert karte waqt auxiliary 'do' drop ho jati hai aur main verb Simple Past (V2) 'recognized' mein badal jati hai. Connective 'if' lagta hai aur subject 'he' pehle aata hai. Option (A) bilkul accurate hai. Option (B) mein 'did recognize' galat format hai kyunki affirmative statement mein emphatic 'did' nahi lagta. Option (C) mein 'that if' double conjunction hai aur listener missing hai. Option (D) mein question ke liye reporting verb 'told' use kiya gaya hai jo interrogative mein invalid hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Auxiliary 'do/does' drop and Simple Past V2 formation.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.subtopic: Yes/No Question with 'Did' Auxiliary (Simple Past ➔ Past Perfect)
questions.question:
Convert into Indirect Speech:
The inspector said to the assistant, "Did you verify the digital ledger yesterday?"

options.text: The inspector asked the assistant if he verified the digital ledger the previous day.
The inspector asked the assistant whether he had verified the digital ledger the previous day.
The inspector asked the assistant whether had he verified the digital ledger yesterday.
The inspector asked that whether he had verified the digital ledger the previous day.

questions.explanation: Direct speech mein 'Did you verify' Simple Past tense hai. Past reporting verb 'said to' ke karan Simple Past backshift hokar Past Perfect ('had verified') banega. 'Yesterday' badal kar 'the previous day' banega. Connective 'whether' ke baad statement word order ('he had verified') aayega. Option (B) 100% correct hai. Option (A) mein Simple Past ko Past Perfect mein backshift nahi kiya gaya. Option (C) mein inversion 'had he' retain hai aur 'yesterday' ko change nahi kiya gaya. Option (D) mein 'that whether' double conjunction blunder hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Simple Past question shifts to Past Perfect with connective if/whether.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.question:
Identify the grammatically correct Indirect Speech sentence:
The judge said, "Do you plead guilty or not?"

options.text: The judge asked whether or not he pleaded guilty.
The judge asked if or not he pleaded guilty.
The judge asked that whether he pleaded guilty or not.
The judge enquired whether did he plead guilty or not.

questions.explanation: Jab question mein condition ya alternative ke turant baad 'or not' jud raha ho, tab formal English aur exam standards ke mutabiq connective 'whether' lagana mandatory hota hai ('whether or not'). 'If or not' non-standard construction hai. Option (A) bilkul sahi hai. Option (B) mein 'if or not' incorrect usage hai. Option (C) mein 'that whether' double connective hai. Option (D) mein inverted auxiliary 'did he plead' use kiya gaya hai jo statement syntax violate karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02: Mandatory 'Whether' with immediate 'or not'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.question:
Select the correct Indirect form of the question:
She said to him, "Where do you reside?"

options.text: She asked him that where he resided.
She asked him where did he reside.
She asked him where he resided.
She asked him where he was residing.

questions.explanation: Wh-question mein question word 'where' hi reporting clause aur reported clause ko connect karta hai (NO 'that', NO 'if'). Question ki auxiliary 'do' drop ho jati hai aur main verb 'reside' Simple Past 'resided' ban jati hai. Subject 'he' Wh-word ke turant baad aayega: 'where he resided'. Option (C) bilkul accurate hai. Option (A) mein fatal 'that where' double conjunction blunder hai. Option (B) mein question auxiliary 'did he reside' retain hai. Option (D) mein Simple Present ko bina kisi continuous marker ke Past Continuous bana diya gaya hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: Wh-Questions Retain Question Word with Statement Syntax.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.subtopic: Wh-Question (Why) with Continuous Tense Inversion Removal
questions.question:
Convert into Indirect Speech:
The senior advocate said to the junior, "Why are you disturbing the court proceedings?"

options.text: The senior advocate asked the junior why was he disturbing the court proceedings.
The senior advocate asked the junior that why he was disturbing the court proceedings.
The senior advocate asked the junior why he was disturbing the court proceedings.
The senior advocate asked the junior why he is disturbing the court proceedings.

questions.explanation: Wh-word 'why' connective banega. 2nd person 'you' junior ke anusaar 'he' banega. Present Continuous auxiliary 'are' backshift hokar singular 'was' banegi aur subject 'he' ke BAAD shift hogi ('why he was disturbing'). Option (C) bilkul sahi hai. Option (A) mein inverted order 'was he' retain hai. Option (B) mein redundant conjunction 'that' prepended hai. Option (D) mein tense ko backshift nahi kiya gaya ('is' retained).
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03 & RC-04: Wh-question inversion removal and tense backshift.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.question:
Choose the option that correctly reports the formal inquiry:
The litigant said to the bench clerk, "When will the cause list be published?"

options.text: The litigant enquired the bench clerk when the cause list would be published.
The litigant enquired of the bench clerk when would the cause list be published.
The litigant enquired of the bench clerk when the cause list would be published.
The litigant enquired to the bench clerk that when the cause list would be published.

questions.explanation: Verb 'enquired' jab kisi person listener ko object banati hai, toh preposition 'of' mandatory hota hai ('enquired of the bench clerk'). Uske baad Wh-word 'when' aayega, phir subject 'the cause list', aur phir backshifted modal 'would'. Option (C) dono criteria perfectly meet karta hai. Option (A) mein preposition 'of' missing hai ('enquired the bench clerk'). Option (B) mein auxiliary inversion 'would the cause list' retain kar li gayi hai. Option (D) mein incorrect preposition 'to' aur double conjunction 'that when' dono maujood hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: Enquired of + Object syntax concord.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.question:
Convert the imperative sentence into Indirect Speech:
The presiding officer said to the orderly, "Place the certified case diary on my desk."

options.text: The presiding officer ordered the orderly to place the certified case diary on his desk.
The presiding officer ordered to the orderly to place the certified case diary on his desk.
The presiding officer ordered the orderly that he should place the certified case diary on my desk.
The presiding officer requested the orderly to place the certified case diary on his desk.

questions.explanation: Presiding officer orderly ko command de raha hai, isliye reporting verb 'ordered' aayegi. Base verb 'Place' non-finite infinitive 'to place' mein convert hogi. 1st person possessive 'my' presiding officer ke anusaar 'his' banega. Option (A) bilkul perfect hai. Option (B) mein 'ordered to the orderly' likha hai ('order' transitive hai, direct object leta hai bina 'to' ke). Option (C) mein pronoun 'my' unshifted chhod diya gaya hai. Option (D) mein hierarchical order ke badle inappropriate verb 'requested' use ki gayi hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Imperative Commands and Requests with 'to + V1'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.subtopic: Imperative Request with Polite Marker Elimination
questions.question:
Convert the request into Indirect Speech:
The candidate said to the superintendent, "Please allow me to submit my original marksheet tomorrow."

options.text: The candidate requested the superintendent to please allow him to submit his original marksheet the next day.
The candidate requested the superintendent to allow him to submit his original marksheet the next day.
The candidate told the superintendent that please allow him to submit his original marksheet tomorrow.
The candidate ordered the superintendent to allow him to submit his original marksheet the next day.

questions.explanation: 'Please' aane par reporting verb 'requested' lagti hai aur 'please' ko indirect speech se completely drop kar diya jata hai. Infinitive 'to allow' banega, 1st person pronouns 'me' ➔ 'him' aur 'my' ➔ 'his' banenge, aur time expression 'tomorrow' ➔ 'the next day' banega. Option (B) bilkul accurate hai. Option (A) mein 'please' ko retain karke redundancy create ki gayi hai. Option (C) mein 'that please allow' aur unshifted 'tomorrow' dono errors hain. Option (D) mein applicant ke liye authoritarian verb 'ordered' inappropriate hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Drop 'please/kindly' when using reporting verb 'requested'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.question:
Select the correct Indirect form of the negative command:
The security officer said to the visitors, "Do not photograph the high court building."

options.text: The security officer warned the visitors to not photograph the high court building.
The security officer warned the visitors not to photograph the high court building.
The security officer warned the visitors that they do not photograph the high court building.
The security officer ordered the visitors to photograph not the high court building.

questions.explanation: Negative imperative 'Do not + V1' ko report karte waqt standard exam structure 'not to + V1' hota hai ('not to photograph'). 'Not' particle 'to' se pehle aata hai. Option (B) bilkul sahi hai. Option (A) split infinitive 'to not photograph' use karta hai jo formal examination grammar mein avoid kiya jata hai. Option (C) mein tense aur structure distort kar diya gaya hai. Option (D) mein awkward ungrammatical syntax hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: Negative Imperatives with 'not to + V1'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.question:
Convert into Indirect Speech using the verb 'forbade':
The judge said to the counsel, "Do not argue with the bench."

options.text: The judge forbade the counsel not to argue with the bench.
The judge forbade the counsel to argue with the bench.
The judge forbade to the counsel to argue with the bench.
The judge forbade the counsel that he should not argue with the bench.

questions.explanation: Verb 'forbade' (forbid ka past) ka matlab hota hai 'mana kiya'. Iske andar negation already included hota hai, isliye iske baad aane wala infinitive hamesha POSITIVE ('to argue') hoga. 'Forbade' ke sath dobara 'not' lagana double negative blunder hai. Option (B) bilkul accurate hai. Option (A) mein fatal 'forbade... not to' double negative blunder hai. Option (C) mein unnecessary preposition 'to' joda gaya hai ('forbade to the counsel'). Option (D) mein 'that he should not' unnecessary redundant clause hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: Forbade + Object + to + V1 (NO 'not' allowed).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07

questions.subtopic: Optative Sentence with 'May God...' Prayer Formula
questions.question:
Convert the optative sentence into Indirect Speech:
The elderly woman said to the young lawyer, "May God grant you success in your judicial career!"

options.text: The elderly woman prayed that might God grant the young lawyer success in his judicial career.
The elderly woman wished that God may grant the young lawyer success in his judicial career.
The elderly woman prayed that God might grant the young lawyer success in his judicial career.
The elderly woman prayed to God to grant the young lawyer success in your judicial career.

questions.explanation: Sentence mein Almighty God se prayer ki gayi hai, isliye reporting verb 'prayed' lagti hai. Conjunction 'that' ke baad divine entity 'God' reported clause ka subject banegi, aur modal 'May' backshift hokar 'might' banega jo subject ke baad shift hoga ('God might grant'). 2nd person pronoun 'your' lawyer ke anusaar 'his' banega. Option (C) bilkul accurate hai. Option (A) mein inverted order 'might God' retain kiya gaya hai jo galat hai. Option (B) mein 'may' ko 'might' mein backshift nahi kiya gaya. Option (D) mein pronoun 'your' unshifted chhod diya gaya hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Optative Wishes & Prayers with 'that + Subject + might + V1'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L07
